description: Master supplier agreement for managed logistics IT services with severity-tiered SLA tables, service credit schedule, and an escalation matrix.
provenance: Modeled on the schedule-heavy master supplier agreements used in logistics and facilities outsourcing, where the commercial clauses are short but Schedule 2 carries dense service-level tables. Deliberately exercises a table of contents over multi-level headings, four SLA tables with fixed column widths and header-row shading, a service-credit percentage matrix, nested letter/roman lists inside clause text, and cross-references between clauses and schedules.

runs.text: This Master Supplier Agreement (the
“Agreement”
) is made on 6 May 2026 between
Crestway Logistics plc
(company no. 03288417) of Meridian House, 4 Trafford Wharf Road, Manchester M17 1AB (“Customer”) and
Ternhaven Systems Ltd
(company no. 09174226) of 2 Brindley Place, Birmingham B1 2JB (“Supplier”).

This Agreement commences on 1 June 2026 (the “Commencement Date”) and continues for an initial term of thirty-six (36) months, renewing automatically for successive twelve (12) month periods unless either party gives not less than ninety (90) days’ written notice of non-renewal.

Supplier shall provide the managed warehouse-management-system (WMS) hosting, integration and support services described in Schedule 1 (Services), in accordance with the service levels in Schedule 2 (Service Levels and Service Credits).

The Charges are set out in Schedule 3 (Charges). Supplier shall invoice monthly in arrears; undisputed invoices are payable within forty-five (45) days of receipt. Charges are exclusive of VAT and shall be indexed annually on each anniversary of the Commencement Date by CPI plus one percent (1%), capped at four percent (4%) per annum.

Service credits accrued under paragraph 4 of Schedule 2 shall be shown as a separate line item on the next invoice following the month in which they accrue, and are Customer’s sole and exclusive financial remedy for the corresponding service level failure, save where Clause 2.3 applies.

Where a Severity 1 Incident recurs three (3) or more times in any rolling three (3) month period, or Monthly Availability falls below 98.0% in any month, Customer may treat the failure as a material breach and exercise its rights under Clause 5.2 notwithstanding any service credits paid.
Supplier shall:

items.text: perform the Services with reasonable skill and care and in accordance with Good Industry Practice;
maintain the certifications listed in paragraph 6 of Schedule 1, including ISO/IEC 27001 and Cyber Essentials Plus, throughout the term;
provide the reports described in paragraph 5 of Schedule 2, comprising:
a monthly service report within five (5) Business Days of month end, covering availability, incident volumes and service credit calculations;
a quarterly service review pack, presented at the Service Review Board described in paragraph 6 of Schedule 2; and
an annual continuous improvement plan identifying not fewer than three (3) efficiency or resilience initiatives.
not make any change to the hosting environment that degrades the Disaster Recovery configuration described in paragraph 7 of Schedule 2 without Customer’s prior written consent.

runs.text: Subject to Clause 4.2, each party’s aggregate liability arising out of or in connection with this Agreement in any Contract Year shall not exceed one hundred and twenty-five percent (125%) of the Charges paid or payable in that Contract Year.
Nothing in this Agreement limits liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation, or any liability that cannot lawfully be limited.

Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately by written notice if the other party commits a material breach which is irremediable or, if remediable, is not remedied within thirty (30) days of written notice requiring remedy.

Customer may terminate for persistent service level failure as described in Clause 2.3 on sixty (60) days’ written notice, in which case Supplier shall provide the exit assistance described in Schedule 4 (Exit Plan) at the day rates in Schedule 3, discounted by twenty percent (20%).

elements.text: SCHEDULE 2 — Service Levels and Service Credits

runs.text: “Monthly Availability” means the percentage of minutes in a calendar month, excluding Permitted Maintenance Windows, during which the production WMS environment is available to process transactions, measured by Supplier’s monitoring platform at one-minute intervals.

elements.text: 2. Incident Severity Definitions and Response Targets

elements.caption: Table 2-2: Incident severity classification and response/resolution targets

cells.text: Production WMS unavailable at one or more sites, or order despatch halted; no workaround available
Material degradation of a Tier 1 service element; workaround available but with significant manual effort
Fault affecting a Tier 2 service element or a single user group; acceptable workaround in place
Minor fault, cosmetic defect or request for information; no operational impact

runs.text: Severity classification is made initially by Supplier’s service desk and may be escalated by Customer’s nominated representatives listed in Table 2-4. Disputes over classification are resolved at the Service Review Board without prejudice to the running of the targets in Table 2-2.

Where Monthly Availability for a Tier 1 service element falls below the target in Table 2-1, or Supplier fails an S1/S2 resolution target in Table 2-2, service credits accrue as a percentage of the Monthly Service Charge for the affected service element, as set out in Table 2-3.
